sections.overall: A strong follow-up to the incredible All In: London. On Dynamite, the opener of New Level & Strickland vs The Rascalz (8.04) was the best match of the week, though the 10 Man Tag main event was not far behind. With the World Title match already set for All Out, AEW is delivering on many cylinders right now!
sections.mens: No Men's singles matches especially wowed this week. Although Darby Allin vs Mark Davis for the TNT title was decent, it was below expectations considering the talent in involved so led to a loss for both.
sections.womens: Megan Bayne vs Alex Windsor was an above-average both, the first time we have seen the former in singles action for a long time! Meanwhile on Collision, Persephone's first TBS title defense was far from a classic against Vertvixen. Athena drops out, as her under-five minute match on Collision did not qualify. Hopefully she'll be back soon, as with Hazuki who also has had 6 weeks of no eligible matches.
sections.menstag: For the first time in weeks, the Men's Tag division is finally getting some attention! A mixture of established teams and newly assembled ones featured. No standout matches but some promising steps!
sections.womenstag: No Women's Tag matches this week, though we do have the title rivals confirmed for a rematch at All Out. This division desperately needs some new teams!
sections.trios: Although there was only one Trios match this week (fewer than we've been accustomed to in recent weeks), New Level & Strickland have quickly established themselves as a strong team. With plenty of other groups circling around, the division is still one of AEW's most prominent right now.
